scientificObservations: The two external e− arrows point Zn to Cu through a drawn lamp load. Zn is negative oxidation anode; Cu is positive reduction cathode. Both equations conserve atoms and charge.
The Cu2+ arrow terminates at the Cu electrode; the former cathode-electron-release microdrawing is absent. Zn arrows lead out of the zinc electrode towards Zn2+ species.
The single nitrate arrow goes down the bridge into the Zn half-cell; the single potassium arrow goes into the Cu half-cell. The former contrary/ambiguous upper K+ arrow is absent.
Lamp load replaces the former voltage-meter-only picture, so the drawn sustained electron path is consistent with the supplied loaded demonstration. The picture does not provide a numerical voltage.

scientificObservations: Central H2O visibly has two white hydrogen spheres; H3O+ visibly has three, with all three drawn rather than a claimed hidden third atom. HCl and chloride have appropriate respective one-H and no-H schematic models.
HCl+H2O→Cl−+H3O+ conserves H,O,Cl and total charge. The two marked conjugate pairs are HCl/Cl− and H3O+/H2O. The red-to-blue proton arrow implements donor/acceptor roles.

The two solution panels now use explicit formula-only circles: H3O+,Cl−,H2O and OH−,Na+,H2O. The former water-like Na+/OH− molecular models are absent. Both schematic examples display matched cation/anion counts and are labelled schematic species models.

The unidirectional HCl example is an introductory proton-transfer illustration, not an assertion that every acid/base system is irreversible. The particle counts and colours do not represent measured concentration or molecular size.
